title: Looker spec for renewal funnel
persona: Anjali, PM on renewals at PolicyBazaar
scenario: Your CFO Slacks: ‘Can I get renewal conversion by city this quarter, broken down by new vs lapsed customers?’ You're handing this to a data analyst. The ask is 6 ways ambiguous: which renewal stage (paid? policy issued?), which cities, what defines ‘lapsed’ (30 / 60 / 90 days?), what's ‘this quarter’ (calendar or fiscal). You need a Looker spec that asks the right questions before a single SQL line gets written.
badPrompt: make a looker query for renewal conversion by city this quarter
badOutput:
SELECT city, COUNT(renewals) / COUNT(eligible) AS conversion FROM policies WHERE date >= '2025-01-01' GROUP BY city ORDER BY conversion DESC;

This query gives you renewal conversion grouped by city for this quarter.

hints.title: Make ambiguity visible first
hints.body: Ask Claude to list the 6 ways the ask is ambiguous BEFORE writing anything. Surfacing assumptions is the whole job, the SQL is downstream.

hints.title: Refuse to write SQL until resolved
hints.body: Add a hard refusal: ‘Do NOT write SQL until I answer the clarifying questions.’ Otherwise Claude will quietly assume and ship.

checks.tip: Frame the artifact as a spec, not a SQL query.
Anchor the tool, Looker, or BI/analytics platform.
Name the requester, CFO, so Claude calibrates definitions for finance.
Flag the ask as ambiguous, it frames the whole prompt.
Add a negative, do NOT write SQL until ambiguities are resolved.
Demand Claude state every assumption it would otherwise hide in the SQL.
Ask for the clarifying questions to send back before building anything.
Lock the count, 5 to 7 clarifying questions, so Claude doesn't ramble.
Define the spec sections, definitions, dimensions, measures, edge cases.
Specify the output structure, sections or a table.

tipIfLow: Every analytics ask is ambiguous. The skill isn't writing SQL, it's making the ambiguity visible BEFORE writing SQL. Strong prompt: ‘List the 6 ways this ask is ambiguous. For each, draft a clarifying question. Do not write SQL until I've answered them.’
goldPrompt: You're a data-spec writer. I'm Anjali, PM on renewals at PolicyBazaar. CFO Slacked: 'renewal conversion by city this quarter, broken down by new vs lapsed customers'. Before any SQL, list the 6 ways this ask is ambiguous (which renewal stage — paid vs policy-issued, which cities, lapsed = 30/60/90 days, calendar vs fiscal quarter, etc). For each, draft one clarifying question. Do NOT write SQL until I answer. After my answers, output a Looker spec with metrics, dimensions, filters, and one validation check per metric.
